theorem.statement:
For every \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq1\),
\[
 mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq 2mr-m.
\]
Consequently \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) uniformly in \(k\).  The upper bound simultaneously controls the two separately minimized endpoint supports \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  The lower bound is witnessed by the compatible family \(o_{is}=1/(mr)\), \(e_{js}=1/r\), for which both endpoint support minima are at least \(mr\).  Hence the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is not intrinsic to exact endpoint witnesses.
theorem.justification: A finite-rank endpoint-face compression and a forced-positive-cell witness give matching linear order in the number of observational cells.
theorem.gap: This closes the former support-frontier question and separates intrinsic support from the quadratic overhead of the explicit flow realization.
theorem.consumer: An audit standard may require only order \(mr\) response atoms for exact endpoint existence, although the direct constructive certificate retains its larger explicit bound.
theorem.proof_tex: This is exactly the claim of thm:optimal-support-frontier-order; apply thm:optimal-support-frontier-order.
